paper_name: 71_Truman, J. E., M. J. Coleman, and K. R. Pirt. British corrosion journal 12.4 (1977)_ 236-238.pdf

alloy.preparation: Steel 1. 5 kg atmospheric-pressure induction-furnace melt using Japanese iron, nickel pellets, electrolytic chromium, ferro-molybdenum, refined manganese, and high-nitrogen ferro-chromium. Cast ingots hot rolled to 20 mm diameter bars; heat treated at 1100 degC for 30 min and cooled in still air. Surface ground to 120 grit.

test_solution.preparation: Aerated solution of 0.6 M sodium chloride and 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate.

test_method.procedure_description: 5 cm2 exposed. Standard saturated calomel reference electrode. Pretreatment for 5 min at -1.5 V; potential increased rapidly to -0.5 V, then at 1 V in 50 min.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Critical pitting potential taken at an anodic current density of 10^-5 A/cm2.

experiments.result_note: Steel 1; plain specimen; Table II breakdown potential identified as critical pitting potential in the methods. The authors note intermittent attack at the coating/specimen junction and possible low values/scatter for resistant materials.
